title: Build pipelines with andThen, compose, and, or

blocks.text: Functional interfaces compose. `f.andThen(g)` runs `f` and then `g`, which is `g(f(x))`; `f.compose(g)` runs `g` first, which is `f(g(x))`. Predicates combine with `and`, `or` and `negate`, and `and` stops at the first `false`.

items: `<T> Function<T, T> inOrder(List<Function<T, T>> steps)` returns one function that applies every step, first to last.
`Function<String, String> lengthLabel()` trims, lower-cases, measures the length, and formats it as `"Length: n"`.
`Predicate<String> acceptedName()` accepts a name that is not `null`, not empty, and either starts with `"A"` or is longer than 5 characters.

rows: names `Alice, Bob, Alexander, "", Amy, Barbara` filtered by `acceptedName()`

blocks.text: Think about the list with no steps at all, and about a `null` name reaching the predicate.

cases.says: The length label and the name filter give the page's own answers, and one step runs as itself.
Steps run in list order: f.andThen(g) is g(f(x)), while f.compose(g) is f(g(x)).
An empty list of steps gives a function that returns its input unchanged.
The null check comes first in the and-chain, so a null name is rejected rather than throwing.
